artifacts.summary: Establishes that .opencode/ is a generated deploy target (same parameterized Lua loader as .claude/, single shared source agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/command-gate-in.sh), that the source file is already fixed (sources common.sh's common_session_id), that .opencode/scripts/command-gate-in.sh is simply a stale snapshot (part of a much broader 38-script gap in .opencode/scripts/), explains the source-store-pass/deployed-fail test split via SCRIPT_DIR/../../.. scan-root resolution, and recommends a narrow one-off catch-up sync of the single file rather than hand-authoring new content or a full deploy-engine rebuild.

memory_candidates.content: .opencode/ is a real generated deploy target parameterized the same way as .claude/ (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/config.lua's M.claude() vs M.opencode(), both base_dir-parameterized through loader.lua/merge.lua/init.lua's manager). It shares the exact same source-store files under agent-system/extensions/** as .claude/ -- there is no separate opencode-flavored source tree. However, deploy-headless.sh (the only headless/non-interactive deploy entrypoint) is hardcoded to ext_config.claude() with no .opencode option, so .opencode/ can currently only be redeployed via the interactive Neovim picker. This makes .opencode/ prone to silent staleness relative to .claude/ (observed: 38 of 68 top-level scripts missing, including the entire scripts/lib/ subdirectory).

When a test computes its scan root via SCRIPT_DIR/../../.. (or similar relative-ancestor arithmetic) to find 'the extensions tree', the same test file can scan a materially different subtree depending on whether it's running from its source-store location (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/) vs its deployed location (e.g. .claude/scripts/tests/), because the directory depth from the file to the repo root differs between the two trees. This is a legitimate design for single-source-of-truth assertions (only meaningful against a fully deployed tree) but produces a real source-store-passes/deployed-fails split that looks like flakiness unless you trace the path arithmetic.
